rationale: The literature supports that global developmental delay/intellectual disability is the primary presenting feature in identified clinical cohorts, with congenital heart defects (CHDs) and urogenital/renal anomalies occurring at variable penetrance. However, the hypothesis conflicts with recent cohort analyses on two points: first, congenital heart defect rates in KDM2B CxxC-domain cohorts reach up to 78% (14/18), exceeding the proposed 50-70% ceiling, while being completely absent in JmjC domain variants (0%); second, comprehensive follow-up studies (van Oirsouw et al., 2026) report incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity among loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants, challenging the assertion that neurodevelopmental impairment is an obligate 100% penetrant feature across all individuals carrying pathogenic KDM2B alterations.

evidence.text: The discovery study delineated KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder in a cohort of 21 individuals harboring heterozygous (likely) pathogenic variants, where all individuals presented with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability, accompanied by variable congenital anomalies mainly affecting the heart, eyes, and urogenital system.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA methylation signature
source.quote: Our efforts resulted in a cohort of 21 individuals with heterozygous (likely) pathogenic variants. Individuals in this cohort present with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability; autism; attention deficit disorder/attention deficit hyperactivity disorder; congenital organ anomalies mainly of the heart, eyes, and urogenital system; and subtle facial dysmorphism.

evidence.text: In a focused cohort of individuals with KDM2B CxxC domain variants, developmental delay in speech and motor domains was present in 100% of assessed patients, while congenital heart defects were identified in up to 78% of individuals, alongside common urogenital and ocular anomalies.

source.title: KDM2B variants in the CxxC domain impair its DNA-binding ability and cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All individuals with CxxC variants presented with developmental delay, mainly in the speech and motor domain, in addition to variable intellectual disability and mild facial dysmorphism. Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals, with additional common findings including musculoskeletal, ophthalmological, and urogenital anomalies

evidence.text: A comprehensive assessment evaluating 68 individuals (with 37 variants in 47 individuals classified as pathogenic/likely pathogenic) demonstrated congenital heart defects in 14/18 (77.8%) individuals with CxxC variants and 3/5 (60%) with pLOF variants, but 0% in JmjC variants. Furthermore, the findings explicitly demonstrated variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants.

source.title: Comprehensive Assessment of the KDM2B‐Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder and the 12q24. 31 Microdeletion Syndrome
source.quote: Congenital heart defects were present in 12q24.31 (3/12) and KDM2B (14/18 CxxC, 3/5 pLOF) cohorts, while they were absent in the KDM2B JmjC and SETD1B cohorts... In contrast, our findings point to variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of loss-of-function variants and JmjC domain variants complicating variant classification and genetic counseling.

evidence.text: In a 3-patient series with KDM2B CxxC variants, all 3 exhibited developmental delay; 2 out of 3 had congenital heart defects (atrial septal defects, ventricular septal defect), and 1 out of 3 exhibited structural renal malformation (solitary kidney).

conflicts: CHD penetrance depends heavily on variant domain: while CHD occurs in 60% of pLOF variants (3/5), it reaches 77.8% (14/18) to 78% in CxxC-domain variants (exceeding the proposed 50-70% range), and drops to 0% in JmjC variants.

van Oirsouw et al. (2026) report incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity among pLOF and JmjC variants, contradicting the assertion that neurodevelopmental impairment is an obligate 100% penetrant feature across all individuals.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true penetrance of non-syndromic versus syndromic neurodevelopmental impairment among unselected adult carriers of KDM2B loss-of-function variants in population biobanks?
new_directions.rationale: Clinical discovery cohorts suffer from ascertainment bias towards severe presentations. Van Oirsouw et al. (2026) identified incomplete penetrance for pLOF variants, which needs systematic quantification in unselected population databases (e.g., UK Biobank, All of Us).

new_directions.question_text: Does the specific CxxC domain DNA-binding disruption cause structural cardiac and urogenital defects via a dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanism compared to haploinsufficiency?
new_directions.rationale: CHD and other extra-CNS structural malformations are heavily concentrated in CxxC domain variants (up to 78%) compared to JmjC and haploinsufficient alleles, suggesting distinct molecular pathology that could delineate subtype-specific diagnostic criteria.
